Rifle soldiers, jumpers, risen soldiers, walkers, grenade throwers, the green soldier, gate soldiers and bomb throwers (5, 10, 21, 23-27, 32) take both; soldiers lying in wait, in trenches and foxholes, bunker guns, lorries, snipers and mortar men (7, 13, 28, 30, 35, 36, 39, 40) only a grenade; guards (17) only a bullet. Prisoners, vehicles, jeeps, doors and anything thrown are never hit.

Points for hitting each behaviour, in hundreds and in BCD, added by $23E7: 3 (300) for most soldiers, 2 for a foxhole, 5 for a trench soldier, a bomb thrower, a sniper or a mortar man, $0A (1,000) for a guard or either half of a lorry, $14 (1,400) for the green soldier. A bunker's gun is listed at $0A, but a grenade that destroys it takes the path at $37B1, which adds its own 1,000.
Behaviour 16: nothing. The second sprite of a motorcycle and sidecar is moved by its leader.

Behaviour 40, the mortar man in his trench. Every 64 frames he fires a mortar bomb at the player when $32CF can (a free slot, the player on his side of x 256), the bomb then made behaviour $0E with block $D0, black; the shared flag $04EA, set whether or not a bomb went out, then plays his three-frame recoil ($CF, $CE, $CD at frames 3, 15 and 20 of the 32) and clears itself. The flag is shared with the trench soldiers ($2BC1), so one man's shot can set another's animation going.
Every 64 frames of his timer the mortar man tries to fire at the player ($32CF, which needs a free slot and the player on his side of x 256) and starts his recoil ($04EA = 1) either way.
Behaviour 39, the sniper: a soldier lying in wait who never gets up. Turns to face the player ($2FEE) and fires ($33B2) on every pass he is allowed to.

Behaviour 38, a door in a wall. Every 128 frames it slides up for 15 frames (dy = -1, the y-speed doubling as its state), then down for 15, and at the turn lets out a rifle soldier (behaviour 5, dark grey) 16 pixels below it, walking out in the door's heading ($04AC, down-left or down-right).
Fifteen frames after the turn the door is shut again and stops.

Fifteen frames after it started up the door is open: it turns to slide down (y-speed 1) and lets out a rifle soldier (behaviour 5, grey) in the first free slot, 16 pixels below it, walking in the door's heading.

Behaviour 37, the jeep from behind: faces the player's direction ($310A) and fires ($33B2) as it drives up the screen, slowing to one pixel a frame at frame 70 and speeding up to two again at frame 140.
Behaviour 35: the front half of the lorry does nothing of its own; it moves with the speed it was given. Also the RTS the routines around it branch to.
Behaviour 36, the back of the lorry: every 64 frames it drops a soldier ten pixels to its right, a jumper (behaviour 10, orange, x-speed 1) whose timer starts at 29, so he jumps on the next frame.

Behaviour 34, the leading half of a vehicle crossing the screen: every 16 frames it moves itself and its other half ($04A1) down a pixel. The bob back up copies the motorcycle's at $2B84, but with the timer masked to its low four bits the value compared with $10 is 1-15, or the y just stored on the frame of the step down, so it would run only at y $10, outside the play area, and the vehicle drifts down.
A holds the timer's low bits (1-15) or the y just stored, never $10 unless the y is
35 bytes of code nothing reaches: a behaviour that waits until its timer reaches 60, then becomes an explosion (behaviour $0C), stopped, with the spark table's first block ($36F6).

Behaviour 32, the bomb thrower: walks in its heading, animated from $27C2 every 8 frames. Every 32 frames, if the player is level with him or below and a slot is free, he stops for a moment (block $E8) and throws a bomb from his own position: behaviour $21 (33), white, falling two pixels a frame, drawn and aimed by where the player is: down-left (block $EA) when the player is 30 or more pixels to his left, and always when the thrower is right of x 255; down-right ($EB) when the player is more than 30 to his right; straight down ($E9) otherwise. The player's x-high is not looked at. The bomb explodes after 90 frames ($2F61).

The bomb thrower throws, if the player is level with him or below and a slot is free: he stops (block $E8) and the free slot becomes a bomb (behaviour $21, white), aimed straight down, down-left or down-right by where the player is.
the same store twice; dy is left as it was
The bomb thrower's walk, four blocks: $E5, $E6, $E7, $E6.

Behaviour 30, the gun in a bunker's slit: every 32 frames, if the player is level with it or below and a slot is free, it fires a shell (behaviour $1F (31), black, block $D2) from six pixels below it and eight to the side it faces, moving one pixel down and two across a frame, which explodes after 90 frames ($2F61). Only a grenade destroys it ($37B1).
The right-hand bunker gun's shell moves two pixels a frame to the right and starts eight pixels right of the gun.
Behaviour 29, a soldier shot in a foxhole or lying down: shows block $CB, then $CC from frame 10, and is gone at frame 20.

Behaviour 28, a foxhole: its soldier rises and ducks in a 128-frame cycle of eight 16-frame steps from $287D, standing up (block $C8) for three of them. While he stands he fires ($33B2), turning to face the player ($2FEE) once he is at y $50 or lower.
The foxhole's eight steps: $EC, $ED (rising), $C8 three times (up and firing), $ED, $EC, $EC.
Finds the map cell four steps ahead of enemy X: its x and y plus four times its speeds, into $04F0-$04F2, then the cell's address ($1711, which leaves it in $FC/$FD).

After $2885: if the cell ahead is a wall or water (terrain bit 0 or 2), turns the enemy round, adding 4 to 11 sixteenths of a turn at random to its heading ($04A1), and sets its speeds from the heading tables ($32AF, $32BF).
The cell ahead was clear: the enemy keeps its heading.
After $2885: puts the enemy behind the scenery ($0442 = $FF) when the cell ahead has terrain bit 1, in front otherwise.

Behaviour 26, the green soldier: walks, turning away from walls ($28BA), in front of or behind the scenery ($28F0), with two walk frames for each direction ($2934). Never fires. Hitting him leaves a score sprite reading 2000 ($23E7).
The green soldier's frames: $B9 and $BA walking right, $EF and $F0 walking left.
The green soldier's frames walking left, $EF and $F0, every eight frames ($291D).

Behaviour 25, a grenade thrower who walks in from the right for 100 frames, then stands. Standing, he raises a grenade (block $E3) every 16 frames and throws it eight frames later (block $E4, $32CF). From frame 200 he turns right and walks off at one pixel a frame.
The grenadier raises his grenade: block $E3.
From frame 200 the grenadier turns right (heading 4) and walks off a pixel a frame.
The grenadier's walk frame for his heading, from the shared walk table ($3CA2), a new frame every four frames.

Behaviour 24, a soldier who throws grenades as he goes: every 64 frames he stops (block $E3), throws at frame 6 of the 64 ($32CF), and at frame 20 sets off again, his heading turned a sixteenth of a turn either way at random. On every other frame of the 64, standing or walking, he turns from walls, goes behind scenery and may fire his rifle ($33B2).
At frame 20 of each 64 the grenadier sets off again, his heading turned a sixteenth either way at random, with that heading's speeds.
From frame 20 of each 64 he walks, animated from the shared walk table; before it he stands.
Every frame but frames 0, 6 and 20 of each 64: the map ahead ($2885), turning from walls ($28BA), going behind scenery ($28F0), and a chance to fire ($33B2).

Behaviour 23, a soldier walking in from the side (handlers 8 and 9): walks in its heading, animated from the shared walk frames ($3CA2), behind the scenery where the map says, and when its timer reaches the count the spawn list gave it ($04A1) turns down the screen (heading 8). It never fires and does not turn at walls.
The walker's timer has reached the spawn list's count: he turns down the screen (heading 8) and takes that heading's speeds ($32AF, $32BF).

Behaviour 22, a box of grenades. When the player stands on it (same x-high, the box's x from 14 pixels left of his to 15 right, its y from 9 above his to 18 below) he gains three grenades, the count is redrawn, 1,000 points are added and effect 0 plays, and the box goes. The box flashes between colours $0B and $08 every 8 frames. The effect request returns with X = 0 ($5F56 loads it from $5526, 0 while effects are on), so on the frame of the pickup that colour store lands on enemy 0 and the enemy loop goes on from enemy 1 ($2495). When the 1,000 points cross a multiple of 10,000, the extra life's effect zeroes X before $3570 too, which then frees enemy 0 instead; unless the box is enemy 0, the loop reaches it again and it pays out a second time, six grenades and 2,000 points in all.
The operand of the LDA #$03 that gives three grenades for a box: the trainer's unlimited grenades zeroes it ($45BC).
The grenade box flashes grey ($0B) and orange ($08), changing every eight frames.
Behaviour 20, a freed prisoner: waves (blocks $C4 and $C5, every 8 frames) for 100 frames, then goes. Freeing him adds no points of his own.
The freed prisoner's two frames, arms up: $C4 and $C5.
Behaviour 19, a score sprite (2000 or 1000) left where a green soldier or a guard was shot: gone after 65 frames.
Behaviour 18, a prisoner: two frames ($2B0A), standing, until the top of the screen passes map row $71; then he walks up and to the left, one pixel a frame each way, with the guards.
The prisoner's two frames: $C2 and $C3.

Behaviour 17, a guard: as the prisoner, with frames $C0 and $C1, leading him up and to the left once the top of the screen passes map row $71. Shooting both guards (only a bullet counts) frees the prisoner ($23E7).
The guard's two frames: $C0 and $C1.

Behaviour 15, the motorcycle and sidecar that stops (handler 4). Coming in from the right it bobs a pixel down and up every 32 pixels, slows to one pixel a frame at x $B4 and stops at x $A5. Stopped, the pair alternates two frame pairs every 16 frames ($B2/$B3, $B4/$B5) and the passenger throws a grenade every 32 frames ($32CF), until the scrolling map has carried it down to y $73; then it rides off to the left (blocks $B0/$B1), speeding up again at x $A0.

The motorcycle in motion (the rider and the sidecar together, Y the other half): for 16 pixels in every 32 of its x it rides a pixel lower, and between x $B4 and x $A0 it slows to a pixel a frame, then goes back to two.

Behaviour 13, a soldier in a trench, shown with the recoil frames he shares with the mortar man ($04EA). Every 64 frames, if a slot is free and the player's x is from $2F to $FF (x-high clear), he lobs a mortar bomb (behaviour $0E, block $D0, black) to the left: its x-speed is ($12E - the player's x) / 64 made negative, -1 to -3, so always leftward, and its y-speed the distance down to the player / 64, less 2; the distance is shifted as an unsigned byte, so with the player above him the y-speed comes out 0 or 1. When the map has carried him down to y $82 he climbs out and becomes a rifle soldier (behaviour 5) walking up the screen.
The trench soldier climbs out when the map has carried him down to y $82: block $98, x-speed 0, y-speed -1, heading up (0), timer zero, and from then on a rifle soldier (behaviour 5) walking up.

The trench soldier's lob, every 64 frames of his timer, if a slot is free and the player is left of x 256 and not at the far left (x $2F-$FF): the free slot becomes a mortar bomb from two pixels above him, its speeds from the distance to the player ($3537), and his recoil starts ($04EA, block $CE).

Where the soldiers entering from the side at the gate start (area 1, $2D08), four ways chosen at random, six tables of four: x ($2CA3: $29, $29, $32, $32), y before a random 0-7 is added ($2CA7: $78, $A5, $78, $A5), x-speed ($2CAB: 1, 1, -1, -1), heading ($2CAF: right, right, left, left), block ($2CB3: $9B) and x-high ($2CB7: 0, 0, $FF, $FF). So two from the left edge and two from the right, each at one of two heights.
The side entries' y before a random 0-7 is added ($2D1A): $78, $A5, $78, $A5.
The side entries' x-speeds ($2D26): 1, 1, -1, -1.
The side entries' headings ($2D31): right (4) from the left edge, left ($0C) from the right.
The side entries' first block, $9B for all four ($2D3A).
The side entries' x-high flags ($2D20): 0, 0, $FF, $FF, so the last two start at x $132.

Behaviour 0, a free slot, which may start a soldier of its own. At the top of the map ($0403 = 0), while gate soldiers remain ($04EF, 20 a life), one chance in 128 for each free slot on each pass of the game logic sends one out: it sets the enemies' fire mask to the slowest ($0504 = $3F), counts the soldier off and makes a gate soldier (behaviour 27) by area: at x $8C-$CB, from y $64 in area 3 and y $3C in the others, except that in area 1 half of them enter from a side ($2CA3). Lower down the map it goes on to $2D63.
a branch to the next instruction
Area 1's side entries: half of its gate soldiers come in from the left or right edge, the place, heading and block from the tables at $2CA3 chosen at random.
Area 3's gate soldiers come out of the fortress door: x $8C-$CB at random, y $64.

Lower down the map, run for each free enemy slot on each pass of the game logic. One time in four at random (a random number's low two bits, $3FE8) it tries: one chance in 256 sends a rifle soldier down from the top of the screen (y $28) at a random x where the map is clear (terrain 0); otherwise one chance in 256 sends a grenade thrower (behaviour 24) in from a side at a random height from $3C: from the left edge (block $D9, heading right of 2-5) where the map is clear, or from the right edge (heading 11-14) where the cell is character $30.
The rest of a gate soldier or a rifle soldier sent down from the top: down a pixel a frame (heading 8), block $9B, left of x 256.
Gives a new soldier his grey colour ($0B), a random start to his timer and a place in front of the scenery.

One chance in 256 at each try a grenadier comes in from a side, left or right at random, at a random height from y $3C: from the left at x $18 where the map there is clear (terrain 0), as behaviour $18 (24) with block $D9 and a heading to the right of 2-5.
The grenadier from the right: at x $13A, only where the map cell there is character $30, heading 11-14, given block $15, which his walk replaces on his first frame.
block $15, where the left-hand version uses $D9; the walk animation replaces it the next frame
Behaviour 11, a grenade thrown by an enemy: flies in an arc, its y-speed growing by one every 16 frames, through the frames at $2EC8, and after 80 frames becomes an explosion ($2ECD).
The enemy grenade's frames, one per 16 frames: $92, $91, $91, $92, $93.

Turns enemy slot X into an explosion: behaviour $0C ($386D), stopped, block $AF, red. Used by thrown grenades, mortar bombs, bombs and shells when their time is up, and for both halves of a lorry hit by the player.
a test whose branch goes to the next instruction either way
Behaviour 14, a mortar bomb: as the grenade, with the frames at $2F14, exploding after 80 frames.
The mortar bomb's frames: $D2, $D1, $D0, $D1, $D2, so it grows and shrinks as it rises and falls.

Behaviour 8, an enemy's bullet: lives 70 frames. From frame 22 on it looks at the map ahead ($2885): a wall stops it, and it goes behind scenery. Either way it ends as a spark (behaviour 9). The first 22 frames let it leave a soldier standing behind cover.
An enemy bullet becomes a spark (behaviour 9): stopped, timer zero.
Behaviours 31 and 33, a bunker's shell or a thrown bomb: moves as it was launched and explodes after 90 frames ($2ECD).
Behaviour 9, the spark where an enemy bullet ends: nine frames from $36F6, then the slot is freed ($2F85).
Frees enemy slot X: behaviour 0, stopped, parked off the right of the screen (x $164) at its own y ($141C) with the blank block $FF. The same as $3570.

Behaviour 7, a soldier lying in wait: turns to face the player once he is at y $50 or lower ($2FEE) and fires ($33B2). When the map has carried him down to y $82 he gets up and becomes a soldier risen from cover (behaviour 21) walking up the screen, straight or a pixel to either side, behind the scenery.
Once the scroll has carried this soldier down to y $50 or lower he turns to face the player ($2FEE); on every pass he may fire ($33B2).

Turns a soldier who lies or crouches to face the player, choosing from three frames: down-left (block $CA) when the player is more than 50 pixels to his left, down-right ($C9) when he is 50 or more to his right, straight down ($C8) otherwise. Sets his facing ($04AC) to match.

Behaviour 10, a soldier who runs and jumps: runs in his heading until his timer reaches 30 (30 frames for one from the spawn list, none for one dropped from a lorry, whose timer starts at 29), then leaps (y-speed -2, block $C6 going left or $D3 going right, one pixel a frame across, the next block, $C7 or $D4, five frames later), falling back as gravity adds one to his y-speed every 8 frames, and when it reaches 3 he lands and becomes a rifle soldier (behaviour 5) walking up the screen.
In the air the jumper's leap frame advances once, at frame $23 of his timer ($C6 to $C7, $D3 to $D4), and every eight frames gravity adds one to his y-speed; when it reaches 3 he lands.
He lands: the walk's first block ($98), no x-speed, heading up, then a rifle soldier (behaviour 5) at a pixel a frame upwards.

Behaviour 21, a soldier risen from cover: walks with the shared walk frames, turning from walls and behind scenery from frame 15. With one chance in eight on each pass he turns to face the player's direction ($310A); otherwise every 32 frames he changes his walking heading ($3237). He never fires.

Sets enemy X's facing ($04AC) to the eighth of a turn that points at the player: right when the player is more than 30 pixels to the right, left when he is 30 or more to the left, straight otherwise; up when he is 20 or more above, down when he is more than 20 below, level otherwise. Leaves it alone when the player is inside that box. Only the facing changes; the soldier keeps walking his own heading ($04A1), so he can walk one way while facing and firing another. The x test adds 30 to the low byte of the soldier's x and drops the carry ($3118), so a soldier at x 226-255 on the left half of the 256 line takes a player to his left, beyond the wrapped sum, as one on his right, and faces right (live: soldier at x $E8, player at $64, heading 4).
The player is below the enemy: the aim is decided by $31AD.
The player is to the right: up-right, right or down-right depending on whether he is 20 or more pixels above, level, or more than 20 below.
The player is to the left: up-left, left or down-left, the same way.
The player is above, within 30 pixels in x: straight up. The tests for up-right and up-left that follow repeat the caller's x test, so they never pass.
The player is below, within 30 pixels in x: straight down. The tests for down-right and down-left that follow repeat the caller's x test, so they never pass.

Behaviour 27, a soldier from the gate: counts himself alive for this pass ($04F4), and with one chance in 64 on each pass stops and tries to throw a grenade ($32CF). Either way he then runs as a rifle soldier ($31E7).

Behaviour 5, the rifle soldier: walks with the shared walk frames for his facing (block $E4 when standing), turns from walls, goes behind scenery and fires ($33B2). Every 32 frames of his own timer he changes heading ($3237); every 32 frames of the game's he faces the player again ($310A).
The rifle soldier stands still: block $E4.

Every frame the rifle soldier looks ahead, turns from walls, goes behind scenery and may fire; every 32 frames of his timer he picks a new heading ($3237), and on frames where the frame counter's low five bits are zero he aims at the player ($310A).

Gives enemy X a new walking heading ($04A1) and speeds: half the time a diagonal picked by where the player is (up-right or down-right when he is to the right, down-left when he is to the left and level or below, down-right, away from him, when he is to the left and above), half the time the old heading turned a sixteenth either way or kept. The player's offsets are tested as signed bytes, so one more than 127 pixels below counts as above, and in the same x-high half one more than 127 pixels to a side counts as on the other side.
a player above and to the left gives $0C / 2 = 6, down and to the right: away from him
A wandering heading: the current one turned a sixteenth either way or kept, at random (keeping it twice as likely, as the fourth choice, -2, becomes 0).
Stores the new heading (0-15) in $04A1 and takes its speeds from $32AF and $32BF.
X-speed for each of the 16 headings, a sixteenth of a turn apart, clockwise from 0 = up: 0, then 1 for 1-7 (rightward), 0 for 8 (down), -1 for 9-15.

Y-speed for each of the 16 headings: -1 for 15, 0, 1 and 2, 0 for 3-5 (across), 1 for 6-10, 0 for 11-13, -1 for 14. Speeds are one pixel a frame, so diagonals are as fast in each direction as straight lines.

Makes enemy X throw a grenade at the player, if both are on the same side of x 256 and a slot is free (else Y = $FF): behaviour $0B, block $93, light blue, six pixels to the thrower's right. Its speeds are the distances to the player divided by 64 ($3537, the signs kept), with two more pixels a frame upward; the gravity in $2EA1 bends that into an arc. Returns the grenade's slot in Y.
No slot was free, or the thrower and the player are on different sides of x 256: Y = $FF tells the caller nothing was thrown.

The thrown grenade: slot Y six pixels to the thrower's right at his height, block $93, light blue, behaviour $0B; its speeds come from the distance to the player, a sixty-fourth of it each frame ($3537), signs set by which side he is on.
The player is to the left and below: the distances are scaled and the x-speed made negative.
The player is to the right: the y-distance, scaled, and made negative when he is above.
The player is below: the y-distance is scaled as it is.
Stores the grenade's speeds, with two more pixels a frame upwards than the aim.

Fires an enemy's rifle. Only on frames of its timer where (timer AND the fire mask $0504) is 0, which is every 64, 32 or 16 frames by area and loop ($3EB4), every 64 once the gate soldiers have started coming ($2CD1), and only with a free slot. The player's place is classed into one of eight directions from the soldier by the same boxes as $310A (30 pixels across, 20 up and down, with the same wrap of x + 30 past 255 at $33D8); the soldier fires only if his facing is already that direction. The bullet is behaviour 8, block $90, white, from the muzzle offset for that facing ($35F9, $3609), at two pixels a frame straight or one each way diagonally ($3517, $3527). Live, a soldier held at x $E8 with the player level at x $64 fired every bullet to the right, away from him.
No shot this frame: the fire mask ($0504) kept it back, or no enemy slot was free.
The player is to the right of the shooter: the shot goes up-right, right or down-right ($34C3) by the player's height, but only when the shooter already faces that way.
A heading has been chosen: on to the bullet ($34C3).
The player is to the left of the shooter: up-left, left or down-left, again only when he already faces that way.
The player is above, within 30 pixels in x: a shot straight up when the shooter faces up. The tests for the diagonals never pass here, because the caller has already checked x.
The player is below, within 30 pixels in x: a shot straight down when the shooter faces down; the diagonal tests never pass here either.

Fires a bullet in heading A from enemy X into free slot Y: speeds from $3517/$3527, the muzzle offset for the heading from $35F9/$3609 added to the shooter's place, behaviour 8, block $90, white, and the shooter turned to face that way.
Enemy bullet x-speed for each of the 16 facings: 2 across, 1 diagonally, 0 straight up or down.
Enemy bullet y-speed for each of the 16 facings: -2 up, 2 down, 1 or -1 diagonally, 0 across.
Divides $FB and $FC by 64 (six right shifts each): turns a distance into a speed for a lobbed grenade or bomb.
Behaviour 6, a soldier dying: 23 frames from $3558, flickering between his falling frames and the blank block, then the slot is freed ($3570).

The dying soldier's frames, read from the second entry (his timer counts up before the read, $3543, and the slot is freed at 24), so he shows 23 frames: $BE and $BF (arms flung out) each alternating with $FF, the blank block, so he flickers as he falls. The first entry is never read.

Frees enemy slot X: behaviour 0, stopped, parked off the right of the screen (x $164) at its own y ($141C) with the blank block. Called when an enemy leaves the screen ($24B1), a box of grenades is picked up ($2AA1), a dying or shot-down soldier's frames end ($3555, $2855), a freed prisoner has finished waving ($2AD6) and a score sprite's time is up ($2AE6).

Sets up the video: banks the BASIC ROM out ($01 bit 0 cleared), points the VIC at its bank 3 ($C000-$FFFF, through CIA 2's port A) and puts the screen at $E000 ($D018 high nibble 8). The character set is chosen per frame by the raster interrupts.

Turns the player's facing ($04E1, 16 steps) one step towards the direction the joystick points ($04E0), the shorter way round. His bullets fly in the facing, so a sharp change of direction takes a few frames to come round.
a load overwritten by the next instruction

The DEC that turns the player's facing one step anticlockwise, taken when the target is less than half a turn anticlockwise; after the two INCs above it, the net step is clockwise. The facing is then kept in 0-15 (sixteenths).
The player's bullet x-speed for each of the 16 facings: up to 8 pixels a frame across.
The player's bullet y-speed for each of the 16 facings: up to 6 pixels a frame up or down.
Where a bullet starts, x offset from the shooter for each of the 16 facings, for the player's bullets and the enemies' alike.
Where a bullet starts, y offset from the shooter for each of the 16 facings.

What the player's four shot slots (slots 1-4) do, by type: 0 $39C3 empty, ready to fire; 1 $3917 a bullet; 2 $365C a grenade in flight; 3 $36E0 a spark; 4 $371E a grenade's blast. The same routines are behaviours 1-4 in $24D4.
The high bytes in shot_routines, read as $361A,Y ($364A).

Runs the player's shot slots 1-4 (X = 0-3) on every pass of the game logic ($08F7): frees one that has left the play area (y above $1E or from $DC down, or x from $15B on), then calls its routine from $3619 by type ($048E). An empty slot may fire, so slot 4, kept for the grenade, can carry a bullet too.
An indirect JMP through $FB/$FC, so update_shots can JSR to the shot's routine.

Shot type 2, the player's grenade in flight. For the first 14 frames of its count, the throw's own frame included, the player's sprite shows the throw ($36DB), unless the stick is pushed, when $3B8E puts a walk frame over it; every 8 frames the grenade's block steps through $36D5 so it seems to rise and fall. It goes behind scenery where the map says. At frame 40 it becomes a blast (type 4): stopped, block $AF, orange.
The grenade lands at frame 40 and becomes a blast (shot type 4): stopped, in front of the scenery, block $AF, orange ($08).

The grenade's blocks, read at frames 8, 16, 24, 32 and 40 of its flight from the second byte ($91, $91, $92, $93, $93): the grenade starts as $93, the smallest ($38A5), is largest at the top of its arc and small again as it lands. The first byte, $92, is never read. Then the player's throwing frames ($36DB).
The player's throwing frames, one every four frames of the grenade's count while it is under 15 ($3669): $A4, $A5, $DE, then $98 standing. The fifth byte, another $98, is not read.
Shot type 3, the spark where a bullet ends: nine frames from $36F6, then the slot is freed.
A spark's blocks, frame by frame: $94-$97 growing, $96 twice, $94, then $FF, the blank block, twice. Used for the player's bullets and the enemies'.
Frees shot slot X: type 0, stopped, parked off the right of the screen (x $164) at its own y ($1418), blank.

Shot type 4, a grenade's blast, 20 frames. Every frame it hits every enemy that a grenade can harm ($2526 bit 1) within 18 pixels across and 22 up or down, on the same side of x 256: a bunker's gun goes to $37B1, anything else to $23E7. So a soldier who walks into the blast while it lasts dies too. Its blocks come from $37AC, a frame every four.
Next enemy for the blast; after the eleventh, the blast's own animation: four frames to each block of $37AC, gone at frame 20.
The blast is over: the shot slot is freed, parked off screen (x $64, x-high $FF, y from $1418) with the blank block.
An explosion's blocks, four frames each: $AF, $AE, $AD, $AF, then $FF blank. Used for the player's grenades and the enemies' explosions.

A grenade's blast reaches a bunker's gun: 1,000 points and effect 2. The gun becomes an explosion (behaviour $0C) ten pixels higher, the blast moves to the bunker, and the map is changed to the ruin. For the gun aimed down-left (heading $0A) the ruin is stamp 3 at a fixed place in area 1's map ($859A, $382A); for any other gun, stamp 2 at the map cell found from the gun's position ($1711). The playfield is redrawn at once ($3F75).
Back to the next enemy for the blast ($3775), X and Y restored.

The gun of the bunker at the right of area 1's map, facing left (heading $0A): the blast moves to the bunker, the gun becomes an explosion and stamp 3, the ruin, goes over the bunker at $859A (columns 34-39).

Behaviour 12, an enemy's explosion (from a thrown grenade, a mortar bomb, a bunker's shell, a bomb, a lorry or a destroyed gun): 20 frames from $37AC, then the slot is freed. It kills the player on touch ($1074).

The player throws a grenade, from the space bar: not while dying, not once the area is won (no gate soldiers left to come or alive), not with slot 4 busy and not with none left. The key is read by REMEMBER's routine at $5F6A, which stands where the 1985 code read $DC01; $EF there is the space bar. The grenade (slot 4, type 2, block $93, light blue) leaves the player's position at two pixels a frame straight up; his direction ($04E0) is set to up, so with the stick centred his facing turns that way, and he shows his throwing frame ($A4) until a pushed stick puts a walk frame over it ($3B8E); the count goes down by one and is redrawn, and effect 1 plays.
REMEMBER's hook: JSR $5F6A, which reads $DC01, in place of the 1985 release's LDA $DC01
The operand of the SBC #$01 that takes a grenade for a throw: zeroed by the trainer's unlimited grenades ($45BF).
No grenade thrown this frame.

Shot type 1, the player's bullet, 15 frames. Each frame it tests every enemy a bullet can hit ($2526 bit 0) within 10 pixels across and 12 up or down on the same side of x 256; a hit goes to $23E7 and frees the bullet. Then it looks at the map six pixels above it: a wall turns it into a spark, and it goes behind scenery where the map says. At frame 15 it becomes a spark.
Next enemy for the bullet; then the map six pixels above it decides whether it hits a wall or goes behind scenery.
The bullet becomes a spark (shot type 3), stopped, its count reset.

Shot type 0, an empty slot, which fires a bullet when fire is held. Not while dying or once the area is won. $04DF counts up once for each empty slot on each pass of the game logic from $FF, set when fire is released: the first count makes 0, so a press fires at once; the next bullet comes when it reaches 8, two frames later with all four shot slots empty, three with three, longer with fewer, and then it stops there until fire is let go. So each press gives two bullets. The bullet (type 1, block $90, white) leaves from the muzzle offset for the player's facing ($35F9, $3609) at its speed ($35D9, $35E9).
The return, reached after a bullet is fired and when the repeat count ($04DF) is at 8 or between firing values.
Fire is up, or the player is dying or the area is won: the repeat count goes back to $FF, so the next press fires at once.

The area is won: no gate soldiers are left to come ($04EF) and none was counted alive this frame ($04F4). Normally that means all twenty have come and gone, but a soldier entering area 1 from a side is not counted on his first frame ($2D08), so the last one can end the area as he appears. Marks the walk ($04F7, which also stops enemies touching the player), draws the gate open ($15BC, which does nothing in area 3) and redraws the playfield, then falls into the walk.

The walk out through the gate, run on every pass of the game logic in place of the joystick: two pixels a frame left or right until x is $AF, the gate's middle, then up a pixel a frame. At y $5A it sets $04F5, which nothing reads; the main loop ends the area itself at that y ($091C).
The walk out from right of x $AF: walking left two pixels a frame to the gate's middle.
At x $AF he walks straight up a pixel a frame, and at y $5A the area is over.

The player, on every pass of the game logic ($08F7) while he is not dying. Starts the walk out when the area is won. Otherwise the joystick sets his speeds and the direction he walks ($04E0): up a pixel a frame while he is at y $A4 or lower on the screen, and above that, up scrolls the map instead ($0404 = $FF); at the top of the map ($0403 = 0) nothing scrolls and he walks up while he is at y $6E or lower; down to y $C1; left and right two pixels a frame between x $17 and $141 (his x is always odd). Walking, he takes the shared walk frames ($3CA2) for the joystick's direction, a frame every four. His facing turns towards it ($35B0). Then the map ahead of him, four pixels across or three up or down, is checked ($3BB1).
set and never read
Joystick down: down a pixel a frame (heading 8) to y $C1.
Joystick left: two pixels a frame to the left (heading $0C) while x is $18 or more (or past 255), so his x, always odd, stops at $17.
Joystick right: two pixels a frame to the right (heading 4), not past x $141.

The four diagonals, read from $DC00 as whole values: up-right (heading 2), down-right (6), down-left ($0A) and up-left ($0E); each also stores its walk table's address in $19/$1A, which nothing reads. With the stick centred the walk is skipped.
the diagonals' walk-frame pointers go to $19/$1A, which nothing reads
The player's walk frame for his heading from the shared table ($3CA2), a new one every four frames, counted in $04E6.

After the joystick: turns his facing ($35B0), then finds the map cell ahead of him, two of his x-steps and three of his y-steps and scroll-steps away. A wall (terrain bit 0) stops him and the scroll ($3C71). Water or a hole (bit 2) and he falls in ($3C10). Otherwise he goes behind scenery where bit 1 is set.
x-high flips when x carries past 255 or borrows below 0, told apart from the 127/128 crossing by the overflow flag

The player walks into water or a hole: dying with $0503 = 2, effect 4, and his sprite moved on into it, to six of his x-steps and six of his y-steps and scroll-steps from where he stood and 12 pixels lower. The death count ($04E6) is set from A as the sound routine leaves it ($0F when an effect plays, $5F64), not 0, so the fall lasts about 65 frames where a hit lasts 79.
A is what $500F left: $0F, or 4 when the effect was refused
Over terrain bit 1 the player goes behind the scenery ($043D = $FF).
Elsewhere he is drawn in front of it ($043D = 0).
A wall ahead: the player and the scroll stop, except on the walk out of the area ($04F7), which goes on through.

The walk, four blocks for each of the eight directions, shared by the player and the soldiers (who are drawn in other colours): $98-$9A up, $9B-$9D down, $D5-$D8 left, $D9-$DC right, $9E, $9F, $DF, $A0 down-right, $A1, $A2, $E0, $A3 down-left, $A6-$A8 and $E1 up-right, $A9-$AB and $E2 up-left.
The walk down: $9B, $9C, $9D, $9C.
The walk left: $D5, $D6, $D7, $D8.
The walk right: $D9, $DA, $DB, $DC.
The walk down and to the right: $9E, $9F, $DF, $A0.
The walk down and to the left: $A1, $A2, $E0, $A3.
The walk up and to the right: $A6, $A7, $A8, $E1.
The walk up and to the left: $A9, $AA, $AB, $E2.
The walk frames' address for each even heading, up, up-right, right, down-right, down, down-left, left, up-left: $3C82, $3C9A, $3C8E, $3C92, $3C86, $3C96, $3C8A, $3C9E.
The high bytes in walk_frame_ptrs, read as $3CA3,Y wherever a walk frame is picked ($2989-$3B98).

The end of the last area: clears the slots and puts eleven sprites across the fortress (x, x-high and y from $3D09, $3D14, $3D1F), seven in a row at y $32 and four at y $6E, all block $EE, red. For 255 frames each shows block $EE or, with one chance in four each frame, nothing, so they flicker like fire. Then back to the main loop's next area.
The ending's flicker, for 255 frames: each of the eleven sprites shows block $EE, or one time in four at random the blank block.
The ending's eleven sprites, x: $6E to $E6 for the upper row, then $48, $52, $119 and $123 for the lower.
The ending's eleven sprites, x-high: the last two are past x 255.
The ending's eleven sprites, y: seven at $32, four at $6E.

Moves every slot by its speeds. The player (slot 0) moves first and his y is copied into the table the raster interrupts read ($04C2). Each of slots 1-15 has last frame's y copied there, then, if it is in use, moves by its speeds, its y also less the scroll speed ($0404, $FF while the map scrolls, so it slides down a pixel with the scenery).
The player's x is stored and his y moves by his y-speed, with no scroll correction; the copy for the raster interrupts ($04C2) follows.
Slot X, 1-15: last frame's y is copied for the interrupts, then a slot in use ($048D) moves by its x-speed, its x-high flag flipping when x crosses a 256-pixel boundary.
Slot X's y moves by its y-speed, less the scroll ($0404).
Next slot, up to 15.
35 bytes of code nothing reaches: frees slot X (as $3570 does, for any slot) and jumps back into move_sprites at $3D8C.
Empties all sixteen slots: each parked off the right of the screen (x $164) at its own y ($1417), stopped, blank, in front, type 0.

Sets up a life: clears the slots; the player at x $97, y $B4, facing up, block $98, blue, not dying. The map restarts at the first checkpoint at or below the row the screen had reached ($3ED0), with twenty gate soldiers to come ($04EF), the area's tables set ($1427) and the gate drawn shut ($15BC, areas 0 and 1). Area 1's three bunkers are put back whole in its map ($14B5 at $88C0, $859A and $8370), the enemies' fire rate is set for the area and loop ($3EB4), sprite block $FF, the blank one every hidden sprite shows, is zeroed ($3E93), the sprites are sorted, everything already on screen in the spawn list is placed ($109B), and the grenades are topped up to five.

Looks along the area's list of restart rows for the first that is not ahead of the row the screen had reached ($0403), and puts the map there with the fine scroll at zero, so a death sends the player back to the last restart point he passed.
Zeroes sprite block $FF ($FFC0-$FFFF), the blank block every sprite falls back to.
The high byte of each area's map, read by $1427 into $0405: $60, $80, $80, $A0. Areas 1 and 2 share the map at $8000.

The enemies' fire mask for the area counter's low three bits ($0504, set at each life's start): $3F for the first area (a shot every 64 frames at most), $1F for the second, $0F for every other. Since the counter goes 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 ..., the third area of the first loop fires every 16, then the second loop's areas fire every 16, 16 and 16, and the third loop begins again at 64. At the top of the map each gate soldier sent out sets the mask back to $3F ($2CD1) for the rest of the life.

Checkpoints, four lists of five map rows: $13, $3D, $61, $83 and the last, $AF for area 0 ($3EBC), $A6 for areas 1 and 2 ($3EC1), $B2 ($3EC6, which no pointer names) and $A6 for area 3 ($3ECB). A life restarts at the first row in the list at or below the row reached. Each area begins the same way: a new area parks the map at row $A5 ($08B8), so play starts at the checkpoint below it, row $AF in area 0 and $A6 in areas 1 and 3 (live).
The restart rows of areas 1 and 2: $13, $3D, $61, $83, $A6. Then $3EC6, a list ending $B2 that no pointer names.
The restart rows of area 3: $13, $3D, $61, $83, $A6.
Which checkpoint list each area uses: $3EBC, $3EC1, $3EC1, $3ECB.
The high bytes in restart_lists, read as $3ED1,X ($3E1B).

46 bytes of code nothing reaches: a bubble sort of the sprite order ($4B-$5A) by y, swapping neighbours until a pass makes no swap, using $D7 as the flag. The game sorts with the Shell sort at $3F06 instead.

Sorts the sprite order table $4B-$5A (sixteen slot numbers) by the slots' y, top of the screen first: a Shell sort with gaps 7, 3 and 1. The raster interrupts hand the hardware sprites to the slots in this order, eight at a time, so more than eight sprites share the screen.
The Shell sort's gap: 15 halved to 7, 3 and 1 ($14); when it reaches 0 the sort is done.
One pass at the current gap, from position $3D.
Compares the slots at positions $3F and $3F + gap by y ($042D) and swaps them in the order table when the first is lower on the screen, stepping back by the gap while it swaps.
Next start position, up to 15 - gap ($C9).
Sorted.

Draws the playfield: copies 21 rows of 40 characters from the map, starting at the row now at the top ($0403, times 40, plus the area's map page $0405), to the screen at $E000. The loop rewrites its own operands (source $3FBF/$3FC0, destination $3FC2/$3FC3).
Copies rows of 40 characters from the map to the screen until it reaches screen row 21 ($E348); the LDA and STA operands ($3FBF, $3FC2) are moved on 40 each row.
source operand, rewritten by draw_playfield
The low byte of draw_row's LDA operand, the map row at the top of the screen, $0403 x 40 ($3FAC), moved on 40 a row.
The map source's high byte, the area's map page added ($3FB9).
destination operand, rewritten by draw_playfield
The low byte of draw_row's STA operand, the screen, 0 at the top ($3F77), moved on 40 a row until it reads $48 at row 21.
The screen's high byte, $E0 at the top ($3F7C).
The random number generator: a 16-bit state at $0400/$0401, rotated left a bit, mixed by an exclusive-or and an add; returns the new $0400 in A.
Seeds the generator from the raster line ($D012): $0400 takes the line's low byte and $0401 that byte shifted left, read again while $0401 comes out 0 (a low byte of $00 or $80).
Waits for the next frame: until the raster interrupt at the bottom of the play area changes its counter ($040B).
Fills the colour RAM with the area's character colour ($40BC, multicolour), then makes the score rows (21 and 23) white.
Fills the colour RAM from ($FB) up to $DC00 with the playfield's colour from $40BC, then makes rows 21 and 23, the score lines, white.

Builds the play screen: 24 rows, black border, multicolour characters, background brown ($09) with black and grey as the two shared colours (kept in $04E2-$04E4 for the interrupts), the playfield's colours ($4015) and map ($3F75), the score line ($40C0) on row 21 in white and row 23 blanked, then score, grenades, lives and high score ($136F, $13D7, $13F1, $13A3). All eight sprites on, all multicolour, with light grey and black as their shared colours.
The score line: copies the 40 characters from $40C0 to screen row 21 ($E348) in white, and blanks row 23 ($E398) in black.
Character colour of each area's playfield in colour RAM, multicolour on: $0D, $0E, $0D, $0D (green, blue in area 1).

The score line under the playfield, 40 characters in the game's alphabet: "SCORE", the score's digit spaces and its fixed "00", the grenade symbol ($3C) and an equals sign ($3F) before the grenade count's place, "MEN", the lives, "HI", the high score's spaces and its "00".
Starts the raster interrupts: the first at line $DF, through the chain at $0406 ($4119), with CIA 1's timer stopped so the KERNAL's own interrupt no longer runs and the keyboard is not scanned.
The IRQ vector ($0314) points here: a JMP through $0406, which each handler sets to the next.

Raster interrupt at line $D5, below the playfield (the first time $DF): blanks the screen with an invalid mode (extended colour and bitmap together), hides sprites 0-3 (block $FF), sets the scroll to 7, a black background and the character set at $D000 for the score lines, counts a frame ($040B, for wait_frame) and asks for line $DE.
Raster interrupt at line $DE: back to text mode for the score lines, with white and red as the shared colours, then the music and sound effects ($5012). Asks for line $1E.
Four bytes nothing reads: $1E, $2A, $3B, $52.

Raster interrupt at line $1E, the top of the playfield: the fine scroll from $0402, the playfield's colours ($04E2-$04E4), and the first eight slots in the sort order ($4B-$52) placed on hardware sprites 7 down to 0 (y from $04C2, x, block, colour, x-high and behind-scenery bits). Selects the area's character set (area x 2 into the low nibble of $D018: $C000, $C800, $D000 or $D800) and asks for a line 20 below the fourth sorted slot's top.
The top interrupt's sprite loop: for each of the first eight slots in the sort order, hardware sprite (7 - n) gets the slot's y, x, block, colour and its x-high and behind-scenery bits.
Raster interrupt below the first four sorted sprites: reuses hardware sprites 7-4 for sorted slots 8-11 ($53-$56). Asks for the line two above the top of sorted slot 12 ($57).
Raster interrupt above the thirteenth sorted sprite: reuses hardware sprites 3-0 for sorted slots 12-15 ($57-$5A). Asks for line $D5.
One bit for each hardware sprite, 0-7: masks the slots' x-high and behind-scenery flags into $D010 and $D01B.
Sprite 1's bit, $02: the third band ANDs a slot's x-high and behind-scenery flags with it ($43FF, $440B).
Sprite 2's bit, $04.
Sprite 3's bit, $08.
Sprite 4's bit, $10.
Sprite 5's bit, $20.
Sprite 6's bit, $40.
Sprite 7's bit, $80, read by the second band ($4294). The eight bytes after it, the same bits inverted ($FE-$7F), are never read.
The same bits inverted, for clearing one sprite's flag. Nothing reads them.

86 bytes identical to the end of irq_lower ($43F9-$444E), placing the last two sprites; the byte after them, $29 at $44CF, matches $444F too. Nothing reaches them. How they came to be here is unknown, perhaps an earlier assembly or load.
Seventeen bytes nothing reads: $29, which still matches irq_lower ($444F) as the copy before it does, then $0F counting down to $02, then $00 and $FF.

REMEMBER's high-score saver, reached from the JMP at $0A4A after a name has been entered. Puts the KERNAL's interrupt back ($EA31, CIA 1's timer on, raster interrupts off), blanks the screen, banks BASIC and the KERNAL in, silences the SID and saves $0EED-$0F47 (the last rank byte, the names and the scores) to drive 8 as "@S:COMMANDO HI /REM" ($083D), replacing the old file. Then restarts the game at $0850. Not part of the 1985 game.

Zeroes the 31 bytes from $D400 to $D41E: every SID register ($D400-$D41C) and the two unused addresses after them.

REMEMBER's menu, run after the instructions. Clears the screen, puts the KERNAL's vectors back, prints its banner ($4660) and waits for T (trainer) or H (high scores). T asks five questions, each Y or N: unlimited lives ($46D8: makes the DEC of the lives at $0996 and the INC of an extra life at $1363 into LDAs), unlimited grenades ($5F80: zeroes the 3 a box gives at $2A8F and the 1 a throw takes at $3909), no falling into holes and water ($5FA8: fills $3C10-$3C5E with NOPs), no collisions ($5FD0: NOPs over the kill at $1056-$106D) and the C= key's level skip ($7F60: makes the RTS at $5F6D a CMP). Choosing T also points the JMP at $0A4A back at the title ($0883), so a trained game saves no scores. H skips the questions. Then L loads the saved table ($463D) and R saves the table in memory over it ($44FF); either way the game starts at $0850.
The trainer: points the JMP at $0A4A at the title ($0883), so no scores are saved, then asks about unlimited lives ($46D8) and makes the lives' DEC at $0996 and INC at $1363 into LDAs on Y.
the trainer: the high-score JMP at $0A4A goes to the title instead of the saver
Asks about unlimited grenades ($5F80): Y zeroes the 3 a box gives ($2A8F) and the 1 a throw takes ($3909).
Asks about falling into holes and water ($5FA8): Y fills $3C10-$3C5E with NOPs.

Asks L or R ($7F88): L loads the saved table ($463D), R saves the table in memory over the file ($44FF) after clearing the screen.
Loads "COMMANDO HI /REM" (the 16 characters from $0840) from drive 8 to $0EED, its saved address, then starts the game at $0850.

The menu's first trainer question, unlimited lives, one screen line.

REMEMBER's instructions viewer, which this copy shows before its menu. Shows the instructions from $4800 a screen at a time: a page of 1,000 characters copied to the screen in reverse video over black colour RAM, so the letters take the background colour, which fades in and out through $47D6. SPACE turns the page; after the last ($47FE) it starts again. RUN/STOP ($4FD0) fades out and goes to the menu ($4531).
The viewer's first page: the source pointer $0E/$0F at $4800, and the colour RAM cleared to black.

Copies a page of 1,000 screen codes from ($0E) to the screen at $0400 with bit 7 flipped (reverse video), fades in ($47B0), waits for SPACE or RUN/STOP ($4FD0), fades out and moves on 1,000 bytes, back to $4800 after the last page ($47FE).

Fades the background through twelve colours from $47D6 + X (X = 0 fades in, 12 out), each after a delay loop of 4,096 iterations (about a frame) and a wait until the raster is at line 256 or beyond, so one every frame or two.
The viewer's fades: in through brown, red, orange, light red to light grey, and out through light grey, grey, orange, dark grey, brown.
Sixteen zero bytes after the fade colours.
The end of the instructions, $4FD0: the viewer starts again from the first page when it reaches it.
The high byte of the instructions' end, $4F, compared with the viewer's pointer ($47A1).

RUN/STOP: fades out, blanks the screen, clears it and goes to the menu ($4531).

The music driver's entry points, a row of JMPs: $5000 starts tune A ($5F0C), $5003 stops the music ($5F42), $5006 turns sound effects on ($5F48), $5009 turns them off ($5F4E), $500C stops the effect playing ($53CF), $500F requests effect A ($5F56) and $5012, called every frame by the raster interrupt at $416A, plays. The game uses $5000, $5006, $500F and $5012; the driver itself calls $5003 at a tune's end.
Entry: stops the music ($5F42).
Entry: turns the sound effects on ($5F48).
Entry: turns the sound effects off ($5F4E); nothing in the game calls it.
Entry: stops the effect playing ($53CF).
Entry: asks for sound effect A ($5F56).

Plays one frame of music and effects. Counts the frame ($5525). The state byte $5519 decides: bit 7 set, the music is stopped (with bit 6 as well, the voices are silenced first and the state becomes $80) and only effects run ($53A5); $40 alone, a tune was just started, so every voice's track and pattern positions and note counters are zeroed before it plays.
Stopped music: with bit 6 of the state the three voices are silenced and the volume set to 15, and the state becomes $80; then only effects play.

The tempo: $5513 counts down from the tune's speed ($5517) and a tick happens when it is reloaded, every speed + 1 frames (every 3 frames for tunes 0 and 2, every 4 for tune 1). Then each voice in turn, X = 2, 1, 0, with its SID register offset from $54E8.

One voice's frame. On a tick its track pointer is fetched and its note counter ($54F2) counted down: below zero it reads the next note ($5086), otherwise it checks for the note's release ($5174). Between ticks only the per-frame effects run ($519B).
A JMP $538F after an unconditional JMP: nothing reaches it.
Between ticks: only the per-frame effects ($519B).

Reads the voice's track at its position ($54EC): $FF sends the track back to its start, $FE stops the music ($5003, so tune 2 plays once), anything else is a pattern number, whose address comes from $5711 and $573E.
The track's $FF: back to its start, with the note counter and pattern position reset.
Another unreachable JMP $538F.

Reads a note from the pattern at the voice's position ($54EF). The first byte holds the length in ticks less one (bits 0-4, into the counter $54F2) and three flags: bit 6, a rest (no note byte follows; the gate is dropped through $5501); bit 7, a byte follows that sets the instrument ($54FE) or, with its own bit 7 set, a slide ($5520, $52B3); bit 5, hold the note to its end with no early release ($5174). Then the note number ($54FB), whose frequency from $5428 goes to the SID and to $551A/$551D, unless the voice is lent to an effect ($5528).
The note's instrument byte goes into $54FE.
Steps to the note byte.
Reads the note number into $54FB and looks up its frequency.
A rest: the gate is dropped through $5501.

Writes the voice's instrument to the SID: waveform with the gate (or without, for a rest), pulse width and envelope, from the instrument's eight bytes at $5591. Then steps past the note and, at the pattern's $FF, moves the track on.
After writing the instrument: steps past the note and, at the pattern's $FF, on to the next pattern of the track.
Done with this voice.

On a tick within a note: on its last tick (counter 0), unless bit 5 of its length byte says hold, the gate is dropped and attack-decay and sustain-release are zeroed, so the note stops short of the next.
On the note's last tick, unless its length byte holds bit 5, the gate is dropped and the envelope zeroed.

The per-frame effects of the voice's instrument, while the voice is its own. Vibrato (byte 5 non-zero, and only on notes of seven ticks or more, length byte bits 0-4 at least 6): the frequency swings up from the note towards the next semitone by a fraction set by byte 5 (the gap halved byte 5 + 1 times), stepping 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 0 with the frame counter.
Vibrato: the gap from the note to the next semitone ($542A - $5428), halved byte 5 + 1 times.
Halves the gap into the 16-bit step at $5508/$5509.
Adds the step to the note's frequency 0-3 times by the vibrato position.
Writes the vibrato's frequency to the voice.

Pulse width. With effect bit 3, byte 6 is added to the width's low byte every frame, with whatever carry the vibrato code leaves (so one more on some frames of instruments 8 and 10, which also have vibrato). Otherwise, with byte 6 non-zero, a sweep: every (byte 6 AND $1F) + 1 frames the width moves by (byte 6 AND $E0), up until its high byte reaches $0E and down until it reaches $08 ($5510 holds the direction). The width is kept in the instrument itself, so every voice playing it shares the sweep.
The pulse sweep, every (byte 6 AND $1F) + 1 frames.
The pulse width moves down by the step until its high byte reaches $08.
Writes the pulse width to the instrument record and the SID.
A slide, set by a note's extra byte with bit 7 ($5520): bits 1-6 are added to the frequency every frame, or taken away when bit 0 is set.
A slide up: the step added to the frequency.

Effect bit 0, a drum: on the frames of the note's first tick the voice plays noise ($80) with the gate off; after that its own waveform, still without the gate, with the frequency's high byte falling by one every frame.
The drum's first tick: noise with the gate off.
Writes the drum's waveform.
Effect bit 1: on notes of four ticks or more (length bits 0-4 at least 3) the frequency's high byte rises by two every other frame.
Effect bit 2: every other frame the note is played an octave higher (12 semitones), so it trills between the two.
The octave trill's base note.
Writes the trill note's frequency.

After each voice: while an effect is sounding ($5527 bit 7 clear, with effects on), $5528 is cleared, so the voices still to come this frame (1 and 0, the SID's second and first) keep their places in the music without touching the SID. The third voice always plays.
Lends the SID to the effect: the voices after this one leave their registers alone.

Plays a frame of the sound effect, if one is on. A new request (bit 6 of $5527) is set up first ($5531). Every (byte 0 AND $0F) + 1 frames the effect steps: voice 1 sounds its note ($5529), which then moves one semitone towards its end note ($552B), and voice 2 the frequency $552C bytes lower in the table, $552C / 2 semitones when $552C is even (effects 0 and 9 have odd values, so voice 2 is given a high byte as its low byte and the next note's low byte as its high) (byte 0's bit 7 leaves both alone, bit 6 voice 1), and either voice's gate can be flipped at each step to retrigger it ($552D bits 7 and 6). When the note has reached the end note the effect stops ($53CF) without sounding it.
Done with effects this frame.
Counts frames to the effect's next step.
Stops the sound effect: gates of voices 1 and 2 off, $5527 = $FF (none).
The effect steps its note one semitone towards the end note (DEC, or INC when rising) and writes the note it had before the step to voice 1.
DEC, or INC for a rising effect: the opcode is rewritten by $5531 ($558D)
Voice 2's note, $552C bytes lower in the frequency table.
Flips voice 1's gate at each step when bit 7 of byte 8 ($552D) asks, so the note restarts every other step.
Flips voice 2's gate at each step when bit 6 asks.
Done with the step.
The SID frequencies of 96 notes, eight octaves of twelve semitones, low byte first; note 0 is $0116. Used by the music, its vibrato and the effects.
Note 0's high byte, $01: the music, its vibrato and the effects read the high bytes as $5429,Y ($5100, $51E1, $51F6, $5380, $53F0, $5402).
Note 1's low byte: the vibrato reads the semitone above as $542A,Y ($51D5).
Note 1's high byte and the rest of the frequency table to $54E7: the vibrato reads the semitone above's high byte as $542B,Y ($51DE).
The SID register offset of each voice: 0, 7, 14.

REMEMBER's hook in place of the game's LDA $DC01 at $38BE: reads the keyboard row and returns. With the level skip chosen, the RTS at $5F6D becomes CMP #$DF, so the bytes from $5F6D read CMP #$DF / BEQ $5F72 / RTS / JMP $0939: C= ends the area at once. Since $38BE runs only when a grenade could be thrown, the key works only then. In the 1985 release, $5F6A-$5FB1 holds two routines that nothing calls: $5F6A points the KERNAL's interrupt vector ($0314) at $5F81, which plays the music ($5012) from a raster interrupt at line $80 and goes on to $EA31, and $5F96 puts $EA31 back, silences the SID and turns the raster interrupt off.
